Delayed puberty The onset of puberty is associated with an increase in the secre- tion of luteinising hormone. There is a subsequent increase in concentrations of sex hormones, the development of secondary sexual characteristics, and an associated growth spurt. Delayed puberty is diagnosed when there is no breast development by 13.4 years of age in girls, and no testicular enlargement by 14 in boys. In addition to the various causes of hypogonadism (see be- low), some of which may be difficult to diagnose, severe system- ic illness such as asthma or diabetes, or hypothyroidism, may cause delay in sexual maturation.
